newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Shekel fixed sharply lower against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Shekel fixed sharply lower against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed sharply lower against the dollar on Monday following the rise of the U.S. currency to a new multi-year high in world markets, dealers said.

"The strong rise of the dollar abroad led to a sharp decline of the shekel. The basket was also reacting to the dollar's rise and the the Bank of Israel had to intervene in the market (buying dollars to support the basket) on a relatively high scale," said Guy Levi of Bank Leumi.
"During the day the basket fell several times to more than seven percent below the diagonal rate," he said.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2870 shekels against 3.2700 shekels on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6206 shekels against 3.6196 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7876 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7949 on Friday and against the mark at 2.0206 shekels against 2.0414 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2830 shekels.
